items.followUp: What is the difference between an IP address and a domain name?

rubric.why: Award for explaining what an IP address identifies.
rubric.description: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network.
rubric.how: Look for the ideas of a unique address and a device/computer on a network.

rubric.why: Award for describing the common IPv4 format taught at this level.
rubric.description: An IPv4 address consists of four numbers separated by dots.
rubric.how: Look for four numeric parts and dot separators.

modelAnswer: An IP address is a unique address used to identify a computer or other device on a network.
An IPv4 address is written as four numbers separated by dots, for example, 192.168.1.1.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the href attribute in an HTML anchor tag?

rubric.why: Award for identifying the anchor's link function.
rubric.description: An anchor is used to create a hyperlink.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that an anchor creates a link.

rubric.why: Award for giving the tag or attribute used to specify the link destination.
rubric.description: The <a> tag uses the href attribute to specify the destination.
rubric.how: Look for the anchor tag or href attribute.

modelAnswer: An anchor in HTML is used to create a hyperlink to another page, file, or location.
It is written with the <a> tag, and the href attribute specifies the link's destination.

items.followUp: Which HTML tag is used to create a paragraph?

rubric.why: Award for stating the effect of the tag.
rubric.description:
The
tag moves the following content to a new line.
rubric.how: Look for the phrase line break or new line.

rubric.why: Award for noting the tag's form.
rubric.description:
The
tag is an empty tag and does not require a closing tag.
rubric.how: Look for a statement that it has no closing tag or is empty.

modelAnswer:
The
tag inserts a line break, so the text following it starts on a new line.
It is an empty tag and does not need a closing tag.

items.followUp: Write an algorithm and draw a flowchart to find the larger of two numbers.

rubric.why: Award for defining a flowchart as a visual representation of a solution or process.
rubric.description: A flowchart is a graphical representation of an algorithm or process using standard symbols.
rubric.how: Look for a visual/graphical representation and symbols or an algorithm/process.

rubric.why: Award for stating that the problem must be understood before drawing the chart.
rubric.description: First understand and define the problem to be solved.
rubric.how: Look for understanding or defining the problem.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the information required and the expected result.
rubric.description: Determine the required inputs and outputs.
rubric.how: Look for both input and output.

rubric.why: Award for identifying and arranging the operations needed to solve the problem.
rubric.description: Determine the processing steps and arrange them in a logical sequence.
rubric.how: Look for the processing or steps in their proper order.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is a graphical representation of an algorithm or process, drawn using standard symbols connected by arrows.
To determine the requirements for a flowchart:
1. Understand and define the problem to be solved.
2. Identify the required input data and the expected output.
3. Determine the processing steps needed to produce the output.
4. Arrange the steps in a logical sequence before drawing the flowchart.

items.followUp: Name and explain the role of any two components of a data communication system.

rubric.why: Award for defining data communication as the exchange or transmission of data.
rubric.description: Data communication is the exchange of data between devices.
rubric.how: Look for exchange/transmission of data or information.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the devices that send and receive the data.
rubric.description: The sender sends the data and the receiver receives it.
rubric.how: Look for both sender and receiver.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the information being sent and its transmission path.
rubric.description: The message is the data being sent, and the medium/channel carries it.
rubric.how: Look for message/data and a medium/channel.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the rules that govern communication.
rubric.description: A protocol is a set of rules that devices follow to communicate.
rubric.how: Look for protocol or communication rules.

modelAnswer: Data communication is the exchange of data between two or more devices through a transmission medium.
The sender is the device that sends the data, and the receiver is the device that receives it.
The message is the data being communicated; the medium or channel carries it from sender to receiver.
Protocols are the rules that control how the devices communicate.

items.followUp: Write three ways to keep an online account secure besides choosing a strong password.

rubric.why: Award for explaining why a password is used.
rubric.description: A password protects an account, device, or data from unauthorised access.
rubric.how: Look for protection/security against unauthorised access.

rubric.why: Award for a length characteristic of a good password.
rubric.description: A good password should be sufficiently long, typically at least eight characters.
rubric.how: Look for a long password or an eight-character minimum.

rubric.why: Award for a varied combination of characters.
rubric.description: A good password should combine letters and numbers, preferably using upper- and lowercase letters.
rubric.how: Look for a combination of letter cases and numbers.

rubric.why: Award for an additional strength characteristic.
rubric.description: It should include symbols or be difficult to guess and should not use personal information.
rubric.how: Look for symbols, resistance to guessing, or avoiding personal information.

modelAnswer: A password is used to protect an account, computer, or data from unauthorised access.
A good password should be long, preferably at least eight characters.
It should combine uppercase and lowercase letters with numbers and special characters.
It should be difficult to guess and should not contain easily discovered personal information.

items.followUp: Why might a developer create a prototype before building the final system?

rubric.why: Award for identifying a prototype as an early version or model.
rubric.description: A prototype is a preliminary model of a system or product.
rubric.how: Look for an early, sample, or preliminary model.

rubric.why: Award for explaining why a prototype is made.
rubric.description: It is used to test or evaluate the design and obtain feedback before the final system is developed.
rubric.how: Look for testing/evaluation or feedback to improve the final system.

modelAnswer: A prototype is a preliminary model of a system or product.
It is made to test and evaluate the design, gather feedback, and improve the final version.

items.followUp: Write an algorithm to calculate the sum of two numbers.

rubric.why: Award for describing an algorithm as an ordered set of instructions.
rubric.description: An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step set of instructions.
rubric.how: Look for instructions or steps arranged in order and a finite/limited process.

rubric.why: Award for stating the purpose of an algorithm.
rubric.description: The instructions are used to solve a problem or perform a task.
rubric.how: Look for solving a problem or performing a task.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step set of instructions.
It is used to solve a problem or perform a specific task.
